stem: Prospective review identifies a clinically significant interaction before dispensing. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Ignore the alert because the prescription was electronically signed.
Delegate final resolution to a cashier.
Evaluate and resolve the issue before dispensing using professional judgment.
Dispense first and review the interaction next month.
Contact the prescriber or patient when needed to resolve the concern.

explanation.core_reasoning: The supported conclusions on these facts are: Evaluate and resolve the issue before dispensing using professional judgment. Contact the prescriber or patient when needed to resolve the concern.

choice_analysis.A: Not supported: Ignore the alert because the prescription was electronically signed.
choice_analysis.B: Not supported: Delegate final resolution to a cashier.
choice_analysis.C: Supported: Evaluate and resolve the issue before dispensing using professional judgment.
choice_analysis.D: Not supported: Dispense first and review the interaction next month.
choice_analysis.E: Supported: Contact the prescriber or patient when needed to resolve the concern.

related_facts: Before dispensing, a pharmacist must perform the prospective drug utilization review required by 247 CMR 9.17 and resolve clinically significant issues through professional judgment and communication.
explanation.mpje_trap: Distinguish this near-miss from the controlling rule: 'Ignore the alert because the prescription was electronically signed.'

reasoning_steps: Match the scenario's operative facts to Prospective drug utilization review
Reject nearby rules whose schedule, trigger, deadline, or actor differs from Prospective review
